findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - CI validates a change to the fake GitHub pull-request allocator.
Adds work: a forced-collision command-level case; F 1 x H 2 = 2; 2 x C = 2.
The reported forced-collision reproduction was temporary, and no committed test forces a train's raw CRC to match an existing change. If the offsets in this stub, `_number`, and the no-create-output stub are removed together, their expected numbers still agree and the suite will usually pass, even though closing the train can again remove the change's pull request and trigger the slow fallback. Retain an end-to-end case that forces the raw collision and verifies the merge result.

stop.reason: The owner chose one more round: write the 20-run result into the evidence and keep one test that forces the same pull-request number

why: The merge-train tests (tests/test_train_land_all.py test_3 and test_5) sometimes make a CI test group run out of time: forge land --all in the test sees a change as changed after the combined check, falls back to the slow one-at-a-time path, the test passes its 120 and 150 second limits, the group retries it and is cancelled at the job's time limit, on Linux at 45 minutes and most likely on Windows at 55 minutes (seen three times in one day)
